entries.title: Acronyms (Chapter Glossary)
do_not_test: Acronym list itself - reference material only, not an independently testable competency.
entries.zero_question_reason: Pure glossary/reference content, no clinical competency to assess.

entries.title: Overview of Anesthesia

testable_competencies.orientation: Recognize the standard phase structure of perioperative anesthetic care (preop assessment/optimization -> intraop airway/monitoring/induction/maintenance -> postop disposition/pain management) as a framework for organizing the rest of the chapter's content.

do_not_test: The definition of anesthesia verbatim - conceptual framing only.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's key_objectives statement is 'Given a patient who requires surgery, the candidate will assess the perioperative issues based on the history and physical examination... recommend strategies to minimize perioperative morbidity and mortality' - this is an exact match to Toronto Notes' own 'Preoperative Assessment' Purpose bullets (identify concerns, arrange investigations, plan anesthetic technique). Causal_conditions list explicitly names cardiopulmonary, anaesthesic (including malignant hyperthermia, sleep apnea), and intubation/airway risk domains, matching the ASA classification and airway-assessment content in this unit.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Communicator - Accurately convey relevant information and explanations to patients, families, and communities
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (role-level record; no per-objective ID exists for this role)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Group's enabling text explicitly requires the candidate to 'Adhere to requirements for obtaining informed consent'; Toronto Notes' own Preoperative Assessment Purpose bullet states one of its four purposes is to 'plan and consent for anesthetic techniques', directly matching this enabling objective.

testable_competencies.history_exam: Elicit a focused anesthesia-relevant history (prior anesthetics/complications, NPO status, comorbidities, FMHx of MH/pseudocholinesterase deficiency, medications/allergies) and perform an airway-focused physical exam (Mallampati, 3-3-2 rule, thyromental distance).
testable_competencies.investigations: Select preoperative investigations appropriate to comorbidity/procedure risk rather than ordering a fixed panel for every patient.
testable_competencies.risk_stratification: Apply the ASA Physical Status classification to stratify perioperative risk and communicate it as a common clinical shorthand.
testable_competencies.consent: Recognize that valid consent for the anesthetic plan is an explicit part of preoperative assessment, not a separate administrative step.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Medication adjustment and fasting are two of the concrete risk-minimization strategies implied by 74-3's key objective ('recommend strategies to minimize perioperative morbidity and mortality'), though the objective does not itemize medication-hold lists or fasting durations by name.

testable_competencies.medication_management: Identify which chronic medications (anticoagulants, ACEI/ARB, oral hypoglycemics, steroids) require holding, adjusting, or continuing through the perioperative period.
testable_competencies.fasting: Apply Canadian fasting-duration guidelines (6h solids, 2h clear fluids in adults) to reduce aspiration risk before elective surgery.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Causal_conditions list explicitly names 'chronic obstructive pulmonary disease' and 'sleep apnea' among the pulmonary/anaesthesic risk domains this objective covers, and 'coronary artery disease' among its own opening examples of optimal chronic-disease care - a direct match to this unit's five comorbidities.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective covers hypertension diagnosis/management broadly; this unit tests only the perioperative-specific slice (BP threshold for delaying surgery, continuing antihypertensives through surgery), a narrower application of the full objective.

testable_competencies.risk_id: Identify comorbidities (uncontrolled HTN, recent MI/unstable CAD, COPD/asthma, OSA/obesity, aspiration risk factors) that increase perioperative risk and require optimization or delay of elective surgery.
testable_competencies.optimization: Apply comorbidity-specific perioperative management (continue antihypertensives, respect ACC/AHA post-MI surgical delay, use protected airway/RSI in aspiration risk).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's causal_conditions list 'diabetes mellitus' explicitly as an example of chronic disease requiring optimal perioperative care; hematologic/coagulation optimization is an implied but not explicitly enumerated risk domain.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit tests only the perioperative-specific slice of anemia management (preoperative Hb optimization, timing of iron/EPO/blood collection) rather than the full diagnostic work-up the objective covers; included for completeness but flagged for scope review given the narrow overlap.

testable_competencies.heme_endo: Recognize which hematologic (anemia, anticoagulation, factor deficiency) and endocrine (diabetes type/control) findings require preoperative correction or medication adjustment before elective surgery.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's enabling text covers 'error mitigation strategies' and systems-based approaches to patient safety; Toronto Notes' own content here ('an anesthesiologist present: the only indispensable monitor', mandatory perioperative record, routine monitor list) is the anesthesia-specific operationalization of this broader patient-safety principle, though the objective does not name anesthesia monitoring standards specifically.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Leader/Manager - Participate appropriately in the health care system
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (role-level record; no per-objective ID exists for this role)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Group's enabling text requires the candidate to 'contribute to the delivery of high-quality health care services by promoting and practicing a culture of patient safety' - directly matches the mandatory-monitoring-standard content of this unit even though no per-objective ID exists for this role.

testable_competencies.standards: Recognize the mandatory minimum monitoring standard for any anesthetic (continuous anesthesiologist presence, pulse oximetry, ECG, capnography, BP, temperature probe availability).
testable_competencies.depth_of_anesthesia: Identify signs of inadequate (HTN, tachycardia, tearing) vs. excessive (hypotension, bradycardia) anesthetic depth from routine monitor trends.

entries.title: Airway Anatomy

testable_competencies.anatomy: Apply airway anatomy landmarks (glottic opening, C6 cricoid/T4-T5 carina level, pharyngeal airway) to support ETT placement and difficult-airway reasoning downstream (supports SU-A-09, SU-A-10, SU-A-11).

do_not_test: Detailed histology/embryology of airway structures - anatomy is tested only as it informs airway management decisions.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's causal_conditions explicitly name 'intubation/airway' as a perioperative risk domain to be assessed; choosing the least-invasive adequate airway device (BMV -> LMA -> ETT) is the direct clinical application of that assessment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Airway support technique selection is a component of resuscitation but this table's content (elective anesthetic airway choice) is broader than the cardiac-arrest-specific advanced-airway content already captured in SU-A-36; included at WEAK strength for the overlapping BMV/LMA/ETT skill only.

testable_competencies.device_choice: Select the least invasive airway device adequate for a given clinical scenario (spontaneously ventilating low-risk patient vs. aspiration risk vs. positive-pressure ventilation need) and recognize each device's key contraindication.

entries.title: Tracheal Intubation: Technique, Confirmation, and Complications

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Airway/intubation risk assessment is an explicit causal-condition domain of this objective; correct confirmation of tube placement is the direct downstream action of a planned intubation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Advanced airway placement and confirmation (capnography as the gold-standard confirmation method) is an explicit component of the ACLS advanced-airway step also tested in SU-A-36.

testable_competencies.confirmation: Recognize capnography (ETCO2) as the gold-standard method to confirm tracheal (vs. esophageal) tube placement, and identify signs of a malpositioned tube (right endobronchial intubation, accidental extubation).

entries.title: Difficult Airway: Recognition and Initial Management

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's causal_conditions explicitly list 'intubation/airway (e.g., C-spine stabilization)' as a named anaesthesic risk domain to identify during preoperative evaluation - a direct match to this unit's difficult-airway prediction content.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The 'can't intubate, can't ventilate' emergency escalation pathway (call for help, LMA rescue, surgical airway) is a resuscitation-adjacent skill shared with the ACLS advanced-airway step.

testable_competencies.prediction: Identify preoperative predictors of a difficult airway from history and airway exam.
testable_competencies.emergency_algorithm: Apply the core stepwise escalation for failed intubation/ventilation (call for help -> 100% O2 bag-mask -> LMA -> emergency surgical airway) without needing to reproduce the full published flowchart.

do_not_test: Verbatim reproduction of the full Canadian Airway Focus Group decision-tree flowchart - see SU-A-35 for why that level of detail is out of scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's enabling objectives require distinguishing hypoxemia mechanisms and initiating management; oxygen delivery system selection (FiO2/precision needs) is the direct management action for this presentation in the anesthetized/perioperative patient.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Mechanical ventilation is one management option among many for the broader dyspnea objective; included at WEAK strength since this unit's scope (perioperative ventilator complications/strategies) is a narrow procedural slice of the full objective.

testable_competencies.o2_delivery: Match oxygen delivery method to patient status (intubated vs. spontaneously breathing) and target SaO2 >90%.
testable_competencies.vent_complications: Recognize airway, alveolar, cardiovascular, and metabolic complications of positive-pressure mechanical ventilation, and interpret abnormal ETCO2 trends against their common causes (Table 3).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's key_objectives directly match this unit's hypothermia content: 'diagnose the cause, severity, and complications... recognize the severity of hypothermia and provide urgent therapy' - Toronto Notes' intraoperative hypothermia causes/prevention list is the perioperative application of this objective.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's causal_conditions list 'drug-induced syndromes (e.g., neuroleptic malignant syndrome, serotonin syndrome)' as a hyperthermia category; intraoperative drug-induced hyperthermia (including the malignant-hyperthermia differential covered separately in SU-A-33) fits this same causal category even though MH itself is not named verbatim in the objective.

testable_competencies.hypothermia: Recognize and prevent intraoperative heat loss (forced-air warming, warmed fluids, humidified gases) as the dominant cause of perioperative hypothermia.
testable_competencies.hyperthermia_ddx: Generate a differential for intraoperative hyperthermia (drug reaction, transfusion reaction, infection/sepsis, hypermetabolic states including malignant hyperthermia) rather than assuming infection by default.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective is a direct title match; Toronto Notes' 'Heart Rate' topic opens with cardiac arrest classification by shockable/non-shockable rhythm, the same framework the objective and the ACLS algorithm (SU-A-36) both use.

testable_competencies.arrest: Classify pulseless arrest rhythms as shockable vs. non-shockable and initiate the corresponding ACLS pathway (cross-references SU-A-36).
testable_competencies.bradyarrhythmia: Recognize intraoperative bradycardia causes that require urgent action (high-grade heart block risk of asystole) vs. benign causes (vagal reflex, drug effect).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's rationale ('shock is inadequate tissue perfusion... regardless of the underlying cause, certain general measures are usually indicated') is a direct match to Toronto Notes' own shock-category framework for intraoperative hypotension.

testable_competencies.shock_ddx: Differentiate intraoperative shock etiologies (septic, spinal/neurogenic, hypovolemic/hemorrhagic, obstructive) by their distinguishing hemodynamic pattern (e.g., warm skin without tachycardia in neurogenic shock).
testable_competencies.initial_mgmt: Initiate appropriate first-line management for intraoperative hypotension based on the identified shock category.

entries.title: Perioperative Fluid Management

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Fluid resuscitation is one of the 'general measures... usually indicated' for shock that this objective's key_objectives references; this unit's crystalloid-vs-colloid and replacement-ratio content is the concrete technique behind that general measure.

testable_competencies.fluid_choice: Select balanced crystalloid over normal saline for routine resuscitation, and apply appropriate replacement ratios (3:1 crystalloid, 1:1 colloid) for intraoperative blood loss.

do_not_test: Manual calculation of the exact 4-2-1 maintenance-fluid formula for a given patient weight - arithmetic recall beyond the core testable concept of maintenance vs. resuscitation fluid choice.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Transfusion decisions are a downstream management action for hemostasis disorders this objective covers; the objective's own scope is diagnosis of bleeding/bruising rather than transfusion-threshold technique specifically.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Blood product administration is one resuscitation option for hemorrhagic shock; included at WEAK strength given the narrow procedural overlap with the broader shock objective.

testable_competencies.transfusion: Recognize indications for blood product administration (PRBC, FFP, platelets) in the context of intraoperative hemorrhage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: RSI is indicated specifically for patients identified as aspiration-risk during preoperative assessment (cross-references SU-A-05's Aspiration topic); induction-agent choice by hemodynamic tolerance (e.g., avoiding propofol/thiopental in shock, etomidate favored) is a direct application of the preoperative risk assessment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Choice of induction agent in a hemodynamically unstable patient (etomidate favored for minimal BP effect) touches the shock objective's management scope but only for this one narrow decision point.

testable_competencies.technique: Identify indications for rapid sequence induction (aspiration risk) vs. routine induction.
testable_competencies.agent_selection: Select an induction agent appropriate to patient comorbidity (e.g., avoid propofol/thiopental in fixed cardiac output or shock; avoid ketamine in psychosis or uncontrolled HTN; favor etomidate in hemodynamic instability).

entries.title: Muscle Relaxants, Reversal Agents, and Induction Analgesia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Toronto Notes explicitly names succinylcholine-induced hyperkalemia as a Side Effect with a defined at-risk population (burns, neuromuscular disease, severe infection, closed head injury) - the objective's own scope (diagnose cause, severity, complications of hyperkalemia) directly covers this drug-induced mechanism even though the objective's causal list does not name succinylcholine specifically.

testable_competencies.nmj_pharm: Distinguish depolarizing (succinylcholine) from non-depolarizing muscle relaxants by mechanism, onset/duration, and reversal strategy (sugammadex for rocuronium/vecuronium; anticholinesterases for others).
testable_competencies.sch_risk: Recognize patient populations at risk of succinylcholine-induced hyperkalemia (burns >24h, neuromuscular disease, severe infection, closed head injury) as a contraindication.

entries.title: General Anesthesia Maintenance and Extubation Readiness

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Safe extubation criteria (patent, protected airway; adequate spontaneous ventilation) is the terminal risk-minimization step of the same perioperative-morbidity-reduction goal this objective names in its key_objectives, applied at the end of the anesthetic rather than the start.

testable_competencies.maintenance: Recognize the standard components of general anesthesia maintenance (volatile and/or IV agents, analgesia, muscle relaxation as needed).
testable_competencies.extubation_readiness: Apply the four extubation-readiness criteria (no intubation requirement, patent airway, intact reflexes, adequate spontaneous ventilation) before extubating a patient.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Laryngospasm's clinical consequence is acute airway obstruction with resulting hypoxia; this objective's management scope (diagnose cause, initiate management) covers the stepwise laryngospasm treatment algorithm Toronto Notes provides.

testable_competencies.laryngospasm: Recognize laryngospasm as a post-extubation emergency and apply the stepwise treatment algorithm (suction -> remove airway/LMA -> CPAP with 100% O2 -> low-dose propofol/succinylcholine -> re-intubate if hypoxia persists).

entries.title: Regional Anesthesia: Principles and Neuraxial (Epidural/Spinal) Technique

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Selecting and safely offering a regional/neuraxial technique (vs. general anesthesia) is part of the anesthetic-plan risk minimization this objective's key_objectives references; contraindication recognition (coagulopathy, sepsis, raised ICP, fixed-output cardiac lesions) is a direct preoperative risk-assessment skill.

testable_competencies.contraindications: Recognize absolute (coagulopathy, infection at site, severe hypovolemia, patient refusal, fixed-output cardiac lesions) and relative contraindications to neuraxial anesthesia.
testable_competencies.anatomy_application: Apply spinal/epidural anatomy (L3-L4/L4-L5 safe insertion level below the L1 cord terminus) to avoid neurologic injury during technique selection counseling.

entries.title: Peripheral Nerve Blocks
do_not_test: Specific block techniques (brachial plexus, femoral, sciatic approaches) - procedural anesthesiology-specialist detail.
entries.zero_question_reason: Regional anesthesia technique selection is already tested at the appropriate generalist depth in SU-A-22; individual peripheral nerve block techniques are procedural specialist skill beyond expected graduating-MD depth.

entries.title: Local Anesthetic Pharmacology

testable_competencies.pharm_selection: Apply LA selection principles (pKa->onset, protein binding->duration, lipid solubility->potency) to explain why different agents suit different clinical scenarios (supports SU-A-25's toxicity content).

do_not_test: Full pharmacokinetic parameter table (Table 14) memorization - background knowledge supporting SU-A-25/26's testable clinical content.

entries.title: Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity (LAST)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: LAST classically presents with CNS toxicity progressing to seizures before cardiotoxicity; the objective's causal_conditions list 'other (e.g., febrile seizures, withdrawal)' as a catch-all systemic-cause category that a toxic drug reaction like LAST fits, though LA toxicity is not named explicitly.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Severe LAST progresses to cardiac dysrhythmia and arrest, requiring the same ACLS-adjacent resuscitation pathway (with lipid emulsion as a LAST-specific addition) tested in SU-A-14/36.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize early (perioral tingling, tinnitus, metallic taste) and late (seizure, cardiac dysrhythmia/arrest) signs of local anesthetic systemic toxicity.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate LAST-specific emergency management (stop LA administration, airway/oxygenation support, seizure control, lipid emulsion therapy) as distinct from routine ACLS.

clinical_source_organizations: American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine

entries.title: Local Infiltration, Hematoma Blocks, and Topical Anesthetics

testable_competencies.technique_recognition: Recognize local infiltration and topical anesthesia as low-risk options for minor procedures, distinct from the higher-stakes regional/neuraxial techniques in SU-A-22/23.

entries.title: Common Postoperative Anesthetic Complications

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's key_objectives ('diagnose the cause, severity, and complications... initiate an appropriate management plan') is a direct match to Toronto Notes' PONV content (first exclude hypotension/bradycardia, then treat with dimenhydrinate/ondansetron/dexamethasone).

testable_competencies.ponv: Recognize postoperative nausea and vomiting, exclude hemodynamic causes first, and select an appropriate antiemetic.

do_not_test: Pain management specifically - fully covered as its own unit, SU-A-28, to avoid double-testing the same content twice.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's key_objectives ('diagnose the cause, severity, and complications; initiate an appropriate management plan') provides the general pain-management framework this unit's acute-postoperative-pain content operationalizes via the WHO analgesic ladder and opioid/NSAID/acetaminophen selection, though the objective is framed around nonarticular/generalized pain rather than acute postoperative pain specifically.

testable_competencies.ladder: Apply the WHO analgesia ladder and select acetaminophen/NSAID/opioid appropriately by pain severity and patient comorbidity.
testable_competencies.opioid_safety: Recognize opioid side effects (respiratory depression, sedation, constipation) and select/monitor patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) dosing safely, including recognizing and treating opioid overdose with naloxone.

entries.title: Neuropathic Pain (Cross-Reference to Neurology)
entries.zero_question_reason: Chapter A's own text is a cross-reference only ('see Neurology, N43') with no independent content; testable neuropathic-pain competency belongs to the Neurology chapter's own crosswalk, out of scope for chapter A.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective's own scope (nonarticular, often chronic, generalized pain) is a direct match to this unit's chronic-pain content, more precisely than its application to SU-A-28's acute pain.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Central sensitization is a shared mechanism with neuropathic pain (CNS-driven hyperalgesia); this objective's diagnostic framework applies to the central-sensitization mechanism Toronto Notes describes here, even though this unit is filed under 'Chronic Pain' rather than 'Neuropathic Pain'.

testable_competencies.chronic_approach: Recognize chronic pain (>3 months) as requiring a multimodal approach (continuing long-acting analgesics, regional techniques, non-pharmacologic adjuncts) rather than acute-pain dosing alone.
testable_competencies.central_sensitization: Recognize central sensitization/hyperalgesia as a distinct CNS-driven mechanism from ongoing nociceptive tissue damage.

entries.title: Obstetrical Anesthesia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Labour analgesia and Caesarean-section anesthetic choice is an explicit component of intrapartum care that this objective covers from the obstetric side; this unit tests the anesthesia-specific slice (systemic vs. inhalational vs. neuraxial options, their tradeoffs and complications).

testable_competencies.labour_analgesia: Compare systemic, inhalational, and neuraxial labour analgesia options by onset, completeness of analgesia, and maternal/fetal risk.
testable_competencies.cs_anesthesia: Recognize neuraxial (spinal/epidural) as first-line for Caesarean section, with general anesthesia reserved for contraindications or time-critical delivery.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Shares scope with the OBGYN discipline's intrapartum/postpartum care content; represented here only for its anesthesia-specific technique-selection content, not obstetric management of labour itself.

entries.title: Pediatric Anesthesia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit extends the same preoperative-evaluation risk-assessment framework (74-3) to pediatric anatomy/physiology (airway differences, immature NMJ, PNS-dominant autonomic response), rather than testing a pediatrics-specific MCC objective that does not exist for perioperative anesthesia.

testable_competencies.anatomic_differences: Recognize pediatric airway anatomic differences (large head/tongue, short trachea, superior/anterior larynx) that alter airway management technique vs. adults.
testable_competencies.physiologic_risk: Recognize increased pediatric susceptibility to bradycardia (PNS-dominant response to depolarizing relaxants), arrhythmia, hyperkalemia, and malignant hyperthermia (cross-references SU-A-33).

entries.cross_discipline_note: Shares scope with the Pediatrics discipline; represented here only for its anesthesia-specific anatomic/physiologic content, not general pediatric care.

entries.title: Malignant Hyperthermia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: MH is not named verbatim in this objective's causal_conditions (which lists 'drug-induced syndromes (e.g., neuroleptic malignant syndrome, serotonin syndrome)' as the nearest analogous category), but MH is mechanistically the same class of drug-triggered hypermetabolic hyperthermic emergency, and the objective's key_objectives ('rule out life-threatening conditions... initiate appropriate management') matches the urgency of MH recognition and dantrolene treatment. This is a genuine naming gap in the MCC objectives registry, flagged honestly rather than forced to a false STRONG match.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the clinical picture of malignant hyperthermia (rising ETCO2, tachycardia, muscle rigidity/trismus, late hyperthermia) as a life-threatening intraoperative emergency.
testable_competencies.trigger_avoidance: Identify anesthetic triggers to avoid in known/suspected MH-susceptible patients (all volatile agents except nitrous oxide, succinylcholine).
testable_competencies.immediate_mgmt: Initiate immediate MH management (stop triggering agent, dantrolene, cooling, treat hyperkalemia/dysrhythmia, avoid calcium channel blockers with dantrolene).

clinical_source_organizations: Malignant Hyperthermia Association of the United States

entries.title: Abnormal Pseudocholinesterase

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize prolonged post-succinylcholine/mivacurium paralysis as a sign of abnormal (deficient) pseudocholinesterase, and manage supportively (ventilate until recovery) rather than administering a cholinesterase inhibitor.

do_not_test: No MCC objective directly names pharmacogenetic drug-metabolism variants; this unit is retained as COMPONENT with empty mcc_evidence because it is a classic, independently well-established graduating-MD testable fact (cross-references the succinylcholine content in SU-A-19) rather than because a registry objective was found for it.

entries.title: Appendices: Difficult Tracheal Intubation Algorithms
do_not_test: Verbatim reproduction of either flowchart's full decision tree - see SU-A-11 for the core, generalist-testable decision points these appendices elaborate.
entries.zero_question_reason: Detailed published algorithm flowcharts beyond expected graduating-MD depth; the core testable decision points (call for help, escalate to LMA, surgical airway if can't-intubate-can't-ventilate) are already captured in SU-A-11.

entries.title: Appendices: Advanced Cardiac Life Support Guidelines

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This is the AHA ACLS algorithm itself, the direct clinical-practice implementation of the Cardiac arrest objective's key_objectives ('diagnose the cause and recognize the urgency... initiate appropriate and timely management'); Toronto Notes reproduces the standard algorithm content essentially verbatim.

testable_competencies.arrest_algorithm: Apply the adult cardiac arrest algorithm (CPR quality metrics, shockable vs. non-shockable pathway, epinephrine/amiodarone dosing, advanced airway timing).
testable_competencies.tachyarrhythmia_algorithm: Apply the unstable-tachyarrhythmia algorithm (synchronized cardioversion for hemodynamic instability; adenosine for regular narrow-complex; rate/rhythm control medication choice by QRS width).

entries.title: Landmark Anesthesiology Trials
entries.zero_question_reason: Historical trial citations/results tables, not an independent clinical competency - matches the explicit task guidance that trial trivia is do-not-test content.
